q: Bus owner holds back workers saying advance was paid and they must work till season ends. Workers want to leave. Stand?
options: Forced work to repay advance barred, free them and casebook
expl: Advance cannot create bonded labour. Freedom overrides contract.
why: Exploitation shield is strong. Debt confines are criminal, not civil.

q: Shop employs 13-year-old to clean non-hazardous shelves after school with care. Factory next door wants same child for furnace work. Difference?
options: Furnace hazardous barred below 14, shop work tests other child laws but hazard bar strict
expl: Hazard bar is strict below 14. Other work tested elsewhere.
why: Foundation separates hazard from general. SI must block furnace at once.

q: Resident plays low-volume prayers at home and explains faith to willing neighbour. Complaint seeks total home ban. Action?
options: Protect peaceful practice at home, act only on coercion or nuisance
expl: Conscience and peaceful practice protected within order limits.
why: Home faith is core. Police weigh nuisance proof, not dislike.

q: Municipality charges cleaning fee from shops using night market toilets vs special cess on all to build one community hall. Which stands?
options: Toilet user fee valid, general cess for one faith fails
expl: Fee needs service. Cess for one religion is tax-like and barred.
why: Money test is purpose plus return. Service charge survives.

q: Parents want children taught in mother tongue and to preserve songs. School says only dominant language allowed. Right?
options: Section may conserve language and culture
expl: Distinct language culture may be conserved.
why: Culture shield belongs to any section. School cannot erase identity.

q: State denies permit for peaceful pamphlets citing vague trouble, allows counter rally with loud threats. Examine by equality and speech test?
options: Fails reasonableness, allows only listed limits, unequals treated alike
expl: Speech limits only listed grounds. Arbitrariness violates equality.
why: Competitive lens checks reason and procedure. Vague trouble cannot gag one side.

q: Police arrest at night without magistrate nod, no memo, family not told. Accused challenges procedure. Principle?
options: Procedure must be fair just reasonable, safeguards mandatory
expl: Liberty needs fair procedure and arrest safeguards.
why: Landmark fairness test protects life. Memos and information are load-bearing.

q: State law gives job quota beyond judicial cap citing Directive need. General candidate challenges. How to balance?
options: Equality caps apply, Directives guide but cannot erase rights, EWS exception within cap stayed
expl: Balance keeps rights enforceable, Directives guiding within structure.
why: Doctrines prevent override. Quota must fit ceiling and exclusion rules.

q: College set up by business house claims minority autonomy after admitting minority manager. Education officer doubts. Test?
options: Needs minority establishment plus administration, paper manager insufficient
expl: Both establish and administer by minority needed.
why: Competitive trap uses late papering. Origin and real control decide.

q: Detained youth not produced for days, officer says file busy. Family seeks immediate production plus action on inaction. Remedies by function?
options: Ask to produce person plus command to do duty
expl: Production cures detention, command cures inaction.
why: Function mapping picks twin orders. Delay strengthens urgency.

q: Compare order that stops lower court excess vs order that cancels passed order after calling record. When each?
options: Stop before excess completes, cancel after bad order passed
expl: One restrains, other quashes on record.
why: Timing separates them. Prohibition prevents, certiorari corrects.

q: Compare law that limits soldiers speech by Parliament vs local order doing same without law. Validity?
options: Parliament law valid, local order without law invalid
expl: Forces curbs need Parliament enactment.
why: Institution matters. Discipline need cannot replace legislative source.

q: Compare fully State-paid school prayer vs aided school prayer with guardian consent. Result pair?
options: First barred fully, second allowed with consent
expl: Funding decides. Total funding bars, aid needs consent.
why: Pair confusion cleared by buckets. Consent cannot cure total bar.

q: Compare pith and substance vs colourable legislation in a State law entering Parliament field. Use?
options: First finds true nature, second strikes disguised excess
expl: True nature test then disguise check voids overreach.
why: Federal doctrines work in sequence. Substance first, motive veil next.

q: Compare basic structure limit vs emergency power claim that all rights can be erased. Position?
options: Core identity cannot be destroyed even in stress
expl: Basic identity survives amendment and emergency design.
why: Advanced guard prevents erasure. Stress tests procedure, not core.

q: Consider: I. Preamble always enforceable in court alone. II. It guides meaning. III. Amendable without destroying core. Correct?
options: II and III only, I uses absolute alone and fails
expl: Absolute enforceable alone is trap. Guiding plus amendable holds.
why: Preamble is key, not sword. Core cannot be hollowed while words remain.

q: Consider: I. Fee for service is tax. II. Tax for one faith barred. III. Trust faith school may continue. Correct?
options: II and III only, I is half-truth merging fee and tax
expl: Half-truth calls fee tax. Service link separates them.
why: Statement I looks plausible but drops return benefit. Others state bar and exception.

q: Consider: I. Any section may conserve culture. II. Only minorities run schools specially. III. Aided school may deny on religion alone. Correct?
options: I and II only, III collides with admission guard
expl: Admission denial on identity fails for aided schools.
why: Collision question needs fence memory. Autonomy does not license aided denial.

q: Consider: I. Parliament alone punishes here. II. State can indemnify martial acts. III. Forces curbs need Parliament law. Correct chain?
options: I and III only, II breaks exclusivity chain
expl: Chain breaks at State indemnity. All three vest in Parliament.
why: Chain reaction test hunts weak link. Martial cover also needs Parliament.

q: Consider: I. Below 14 hazard barred. II. Trafficking consent valid. III. Production order cures illegal detention. Correct?
options: I and III only, II treats consent as cure and fails
expl: Consent never cures trafficking. Other two state rescue and remedy.
why: Everything-looks-correct hides one poison. Coercion voids consent.
